Just got some time to look into this problem... I did some test and could confirm this. This problem only seems to happen with OneDrive Personal. I was unable to reproduce it on OD for Business and from @JRman your Drive ID format included in your log I suppose you're using OD for Personal as well. Am I correct?

I remembered we could use both `/root:/path/to/file` and `/root:/path/to/file:` to address an item by path, although the [docs](https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/docs/api-reference/v1.0/resources/driveitem) seem to mention the latter only when there's some suffix, e.g. `/root:/path/to/file:/createUploadSession`. I tried adding the trailing colon and that fixed the problem.

I've created a test version [here](https://beta.rclone.org/branch/v1.44-037-g638cea21-onedrive-path-workaround-2720-beta/). Could you help test it? Thanks!

My syncs are all running clean now (windows version FYI)

issue.title: OneDrive Personal throws "generalException" when handling filenames ending with "drive"

repository.name: onedrive-api-docs
repository.description: Official documentation for the OneDrive API

issue.body:
#### Category
- [ ] Question
- [ ] Documentation issue
- [x] Bug

#### Expected or Desired Behavior

The API should work for the files whose names end with `drive` when they are addressed by their paths.

#### Observed Behavior

The query

```
GET /v1.0/drives/71a96798e7b1d253/root:/test/adrive
```

which is constructed according to the docs "By file system path using `/drive/root:/path/to/file`"

returns

```
{
  "error": {
    "code": "generalException",
    "message": "Could not find a property named 'quota' on type 'oneDrive.item'.",
    "innerError": {
      "request-id": "7001728a-4c8d-48d6-96cc-3dfc31de0d18",
      "date": "2018-11-03T16:49:46"
    }
  }
}
```

However, if a trailing colon is added to the original query:

```
GET /v1.0/drives/71a96798e7b1d253/root:/test/adrive:
```

it returns the correct DriveItem.

The date and request ID can be found in the response data sample above, and it seems this only happens for OneDrive Personal.

#### Steps to Reproduce

This bug can be reproduced by the following steps:

1. In OneDrive Personal, create a folder ending with `drive`, for example `adrive`.
1. Send the request `GET /v1.0/me/drive/root:/path/to/adrive:` to confirm the item exists
1. Send the request `GET /v1.0/me/drive/root:/path/to/adrive` to see the `generalException`

This is a summary of a bug from rclone. The original discussions can be found on the rclone [forum](https://forum.rclone.org/t/onedrive-could-not-find-a-property-named-quota-on-type-onedrive-item/7403/6) and in the rclone [issue](https://github.com/ncw/rclone/issues/2720).

body: I have created an upstream issue and let's see if this can be fixed by OneDrive.
This happens to me, too. Exactly the same.

A similar thing happened to me. The name of a folder on OneDrive Personal "Old_drive" gave me the same "Could not find a property named 'quota' on type 'oneDrive.item'." error, and no files would sync. I changed the name of the remote folder to "Old_drv", and the sync went without errors.

The Rclone Developers

#### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

Cannot ls item for some folders

#### What is your rclone version (output from `rclone version`)

1.46

#### Which OS you are using and how many bits (eg Windows 7, 64 bit)

Ubuntu 18.04.2

####  Which cloud storage system are you using? (eg Google Drive)

Onedrive business

#### The command you were trying to run (eg `rclone copy /tmp remote:tmp`)

rclone ls

#### A log from the command with the `-vv` flag (eg output from `rclone -vv copy /tmp remote:tmp`)

See below for longer description

---

My apologies in advance because I believe this bug is not reproducible since I believe it's only happens for a particular folder I happen to be working on.

Recently, when I try to run the command:

`rclone ls onedrive:path/to/this/strange/folder`

it tells me

```
2019/03/09 23:52:16 Failed to create file system for "qx:backup/phone/photo": "photo": is a not a regular file

```

Use `-vv --dump headers --dump bodies` enables me to locate the following error (I removed two sensitive pieces of information and used the placeholders `my_drive_id` and `my_path_id`):

```
2019/03/09 23:52:16 DEBUG : HTTP REQUEST (req 0xc000606100)

Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000
X-Ms-Ags-Diagnostic: {"ServerInfo":{"DataCenter":"East US","Slice":"SliceC","Ring":"5","ScaleUnit":"002","RoleInstance":"AGSFE_IN_51","ADSiteName":"EUS"}}

1de
{{
  "error": {
    "code": "BadRequest",
    "message": "The Path property 'drives('b%my_drive_id')/items('my_path_id%3A')/photo' of ODataMessageWriterSetting.ODataUri must end with the navigation property which the contained elements being written belong to.",
    "innerError": {
      "request-id": "3f4dee5b-dee4-48ab-804d-2797e609c1f5",
      "date": "2019-03-10T04:52:16"
    }
  }
}
0

2019/03/09 23:52:16 DEBUG : <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<
2019/03/09 23:52:16 DEBUG : Couldn't decode error response: invalid character '{' looking for beginning of object key string
```

I believe I found the answer to this after I looked up Onedrive's api reference here: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/driveitem-get?view=graph-rest-1.0

## Possible cause of the problem

Currently, rclone uses the following URL scheme, which works but I couldn't find matching ones in the official api reference:

```
GET /drives/{drive-id}/items/{item-id}:/{item-path}
```

---

The following is taken from the api reference, as we can see the above URL scheme used by rclone as of v1.46 is found nowhere here

```
GET /drives/{drive-id}/items/{item-id}
GET /drives/{drive-id}/root:/{item-path}
GET /groups/{group-id}/drive/items/{item-id}
GET /groups/{group-id}/drive/root:/{item-path}
GET /me/drive/items/{item-id}
GET /me/drive/root:/{item-path}
GET /sites/{siteId}/drive/items/{itemId}
GET /sites/{siteId}/drive/root:/{item-path}
GET /users/{userId}/drive/items/{itemId}
GET /users/{userId}/drive/root:/{item-path}
```

I am able to verify this in microsofts' [graph explorer](https://developer.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/graph-explorer), meaning that: given the folder that I had problem with,

- doing `GET /drives/{drive-id}/items/{item-id}:/{item-path}` gives me the exact error that I encountered in rclone
- removing the last segment, and doing `GET /drives/{drive-id}/items/{item-id}` produces correct response

Again, sorry about this bug being not reproducible, since I cannot share my onedrive folder id here.
